newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes lower despite BOK dlr sales.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes lower despite BOK dlr sales.

text.p: Advance dollar buying to prepare for future importer deals sent the South Korean won to a lower close on Thursday despite central bank intervention to support the local currency, dealers said.
The won closed trading at 864.30 after opening at an intraday high of 862.40. It touched a low of 864.50.
"Dollar demand was strong as traders expect huge importer deals on Friday and early next week," said a dealer.
The central bank offered to sell dollars in three- and six-month forward trading and later sold dollars on the spot market as the won fell to 863.00, dealers said.
The central bank refused to comment on the talk.
Some traders said a correction in the dollar/yen rates in world markets could limit the won's decline.
"Without a rebound in the dollar/yen rate, there will be no further big drop of the won for some time," said a foreign bank dealer.
Dealers saw the won's base mid-rate for Friday at 863.90, compared with Thursday's 862.40.
